title: Drug-induced cholestasis assay in primary hepatocytes
author: Van Brantegem, Chatterjee, et al.
materials: 1.Aspirate the culture medium.2.Wash the wells twice with 250 µL prewarmed incubation buffer. Aspirate the remaining buffer.3.Add 125 µL prewarmed incubation buffer to each well and keep the plate at 37°C for 1 h.4.In the meantime, prepare the calibration curve in incubation buffer (range 5 µM–500 µM) and preheat a water bath to 85°C.5.Prepare the color reagent by mixing solution A and B in a 2:1 ratio.Note: prepare and use the color reagent immediately.6.After 1 h incubation, transfer 60 µL of the incubation buffer in every well of cells, blank and calibration curve to a 96-well thermostable plate.7.Add 240 µL color reagent to each well.8.Cover the plate with an aluminum cover slip to avoid evaporation.9.Heat the plate with the incubation mixture to 85°C in a water bath for 20 min.Note: as heat is a crucial parameter for the reaction to occur, make sure the temperature is constant during the incubation.10.Cool the plate down for 5 to 10 min at 4°C.11.Transfer 250 µL of each well to a transparent 96-well plate and measure the absorbance at 525 nm and room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare collagen coating solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the 3.5 mg/mL rat tail collagen stock with 0.02 M acetic acid to obtain a fresh 50 µg/mL collagen solution.

steps.title: Coat 48-well plates with collagen
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of the 50 µg/mL collagen solution to each well of a 48‑well plate, then incubate at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator for at least 1 h (preferably overnight). Perform this coating on the day before seeding.

steps.title: Thaw and resuspend hepatocytes
steps.instruction: Under a laminar‑flow cabinet, thaw cryovials of primary hepatocytes and resuspend them using a Percoll‑based protocol.

substeps.instruction: Add 16 mL of 90 % Percoll® and 25 mL thawing medium to a 50 mL Falcon tube; pre‑warm the mixture in a 37 °C water bath.
Remove cryovials from liquid nitrogen or freezer, wearing appropriate PPE, and warm them in a 37 °C water bath with gentle swirling until ice melts.
Open vials in the cabinet and transfer the cell suspension to the Percoll‑thawing medium mixture.
Rinse each cryovial with 1 mL thawing medium and bring the total volume of the tube to 50 mL.
Close the tube and gently invert 2–3 times to resuspend.
Centrifuge at room temperature for 20 min at 168 × g.
Aspirate supernatant, then gently loosen the pellet (do not add medium before loosening).
Add 20 mL pre‑warmed thawing medium, invert 2–3 times, and centrifuge 5 min at 100 × g at room temperature.
Aspirate medium and resuspend the pellet as described above.
Add 2–5 mL seeding medium (≈3 mL per 10 × 10⁶ cells).
Determine total cell number and viability with Trypan blue; viability must be ≥70 %.

steps.title: Seed hepatocytes onto coated plates
steps.instruction: Seed the viable hepatocytes onto the collagen‑coated 48‑well plate and begin culture.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the collagen solution from the wells and wash three times with 250 µL pre‑warmed sterile PBS.
Dilute the cell suspension to 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL with seeding medium.
Dispense 250 µL of the suspension into each well; move the plate orthogonally (not circularly) to distribute cells evenly.
Optionally, inspect one well under a microscope to confirm appropriate density and adjust volume or dilution if needed.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C, humidified, 5 % CO₂ for 24 h.
Start thawing Matrigel™ overnight in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Overlay cells with Matrigel and culture
steps.instruction: Add Matrigel overlay, incubate, and maintain daily medium changes.

substeps.instruction: Rigorously shake the plate and aspirate any non‑adherent cells.
Add 250 µL of diluted Matrigel™ solution to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C, humidified, 5 % CO₂ for 24 h.
Replace the medium daily with pre‑warmed culture medium.

steps.title: Perform CDFDA fluorescence imaging
steps.instruction: Prepare the fluorescence microscope and image bile canaliculi using CDFDA staining.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the fluorescence microscope, set excitation λ_ex = 490 nm and emission λ_em = 520 nm, and allow ~20 min warm‑up.
Wash a selected well twice with pre‑warmed standard buffer.
Pre‑incubate the well with 250 µL standard buffer at 37 °C for 10 min.
Aspirate the buffer and incubate with 250 µL of 4 µM CDFDA in standard buffer at 37 °C for 10 min.
Aspirate the CDFDA solution.
Darken the microscope room.
Focus on the cells with the light microscope, capture images of the area of interest.
Switch off the light‑microscope lamp (keep the fluorescence lamp on), keep the plate position unchanged, readjust focus if needed, and acquire fluorescence images.

steps.title: Preincubate and treat cells with test compounds
steps.instruction: Expose cells to test compounds with or without the bile‑salt mixture for the assay.

substeps.instruction: On day 5, aspirate the culture medium and pre‑incubate cells with solution 1, solution 6, or solution 8 for 2 h (allows compound interaction).
After 2 h, aspirate the pre‑incubation solution and immediately add the treatment solution (solution 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9) for a further 22 h.

Typical total incubation time is 24 h; for longer exposures (e.g., 48 h) replace the medium after the first 24 h (day 6) with fresh medium containing the same concentrations of test compound and bile salts.

steps.title: Collect incubation buffer and run urea assay
steps.instruction: Perform the colorimetric diacetyl‑monoxime urea assay on incubation buffer collected from the cells.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the culture medium.
Wash each well twice with 250 µL pre‑warmed incubation buffer and aspirate the residual buffer.
Add 125 µL pre‑warmed incubation buffer to each well and incubate the plate at 37 °C for 1 h.
While incubating, prepare a urea calibration curve in incubation buffer covering 5 µM–500 µM and pre‑heat a water bath to 85 °C.
Prepare the color reagent by mixing solution A and solution B in a 2:1 ratio; use immediately.
After the 1 h incubation, transfer 60 µL of incubation buffer from each cell well, blank, and calibration standards into a 96‑well thermostable plate.
Add 240 µL of the freshly prepared color reagent to each well.
Cover the plate with an aluminum foil seal to prevent evaporation.
Heat the plate in the 85 °C water bath for 20 min, ensuring constant temperature.
Cool the plate at 4 °C for 5–10 min.
Transfer 250 µL from each well to a transparent 96‑well plate and measure absorbance at 525 nm at room temperature.

steps.title: Analyze data and calculate DICI and SM
steps.instruction: Process absorbance data to obtain urea concentrations and compute assay endpoints.

substeps.instruction: Subtract the mean absorbance of the blank from all sample values.
Fit the calibration standards with linear regression to generate a calibration curve.
Convert each sample absorbance to urea concentration using the calibration curve.
For each experimental condition, calculate the mean concentration and standard deviation.
Calculate the DICI using the provided formula: DICI = urea formation (test compound + bile salts) / urea formation (test compound).
Determine the safety margin (SM) as: SM = highest concentration with DICI ≥ 0.78 ÷ Cmax,total (µM), where Cmax,total is the reported or predicted total peak plasma concentration in humans.
